chunks: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful.
Indeed, the deeds of the children are [judged] by the bad deeds of their fathers, and indeed, the deeds of the fathers are [judged] by the good deeds of their children.
This is what has been transmitted regarding that matter.
ai.seo_question: How do the deeds of parents and children affect each other in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq elaborates on the principle of *ta'liq al-'amal* (hanging of deeds), explaining how the spiritual merit or burden of a parent can be transferred to their offspring, contingent upon the child's own actions and divine decree. This concept underscores the interconnectedness of familial piety in Shia eschatology, highlighting that while individual accountability is primary, the righteous conduct of children can serve as a means of intercession or relief for their parents' sins.
